fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 has a new exact kernel. For every degree-≤2 character f, f(000)=f(001)+f(010)+f(100)-f(011)-f(101)-f(110)+f(111), so the forbidden label is replaced using legal labels while preserving normalization, singleton moments, and pair moments globally. Under the existing anchors this costs only baseline+24, making the proposed baseline+8 kill threshold unsound and leaving no asymptotic gap.

Proposal 2 supplies no uniform polynomial certificate-degree or coefficient bound. Degree growing linearly with the variable count makes the full monomial table exponential, while success at degrees 2–4 on one four-variable formula would not discriminate this asymptotic obstruction.

Proposal 3 never defines a fixed-target residual that is zero for every satisfying local label yet cannot be absorbed by shared variables. B_h uniqueness applies only inside an asserted coefficient bound, and a mod-q linear code amplifies only nonzero messages; it cannot remove exact residual kernels or justify the bound at an n^c soundness radius.

Proposal 4 makes only nonzero algebraic residuals expensive and therefore assumes away the central global zero-kernel problem. No explicit gluing equations, polynomial-bit field family, rational Euclidean realization, or proof that every unsatisfiable short vector has nonzero residual is supplied; testing one known identity would not discriminate these failures.

Proposal 5 provides neither a chain complex nor an attachment theorem showing that falsification maps to nonzero homology while honest changes are boundaries. The proposed construction and acceptance thresholds are unspecified, so SNF on an arbitrarily chosen incidence complex would not test the claimed mechanism.

Proposal 6 has exponential assignment state in general; the 16-state four-variable example does not address polynomial size. It also gives no explicit fixed-target geometry excluding signed flows and circulations, so finite flow enumeration cannot rescue the reduction route.

Proposal 7 gives no finite Gram-entry or target-denominator bounds, making its proposed enumeration unbounded, and no explicit gluing or forbidden-label penalty is defined. Even a successful constant-dimensional shell search would establish neither overlap soundness nor shell separation large enough relative to the aggregate completeness radius.
evidence: The Generation-7 verifier establishes an unrestricted exact zero-residual signed-selector attack at squared distance 80 versus baseline 72. Therefore any mechanism that merely reweights a residual must first exclude exact affine kernels.

The degree-2 proposal does distinguish the specific 011+100−111 identity, but the displayed seven-term degree-3 parity identity is exactly invisible to all degree-≤2 Fourier rows and shared pair moments. This is an algebraic obstruction, not finite experimental extrapolation.

Generation 5 exhaustively found short private-row overlap circuits in all 5,832 tested systems, while Generation 6 was invalidated because its constraints were external and an unrestricted mod-2 bypass existed. None of Proposals 3–7 emits a concrete basis resolving both findings.

All supplied successful searches are finite local facts, and the verified ratios are constant-instance quantities. No proposal supplies a polynomial-size family, composition theorem, or dimension-dependent soundness bound.
next_experiment: None for these proposals. Reopen only with an explicit polynomial-size fixed-target basis and target that defeats both the full degree-3 parity replacement of 000 and unrestricted overlap/modular kernels; then prescribe one exact unrestricted-CVP audit on the nine-clause obstruction and a fixed satisfiable overlapping control with numerical pass/fail thresholds.
